key_insight: AutoEnergyDesign uses an LLM agent to optimize building energy systems, reaching a roughly €3.53 million net present cost with far fewer simulations than conventional search baselines.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce simulation costs when sizing integrated energy technologies, including photovoltaics, batteries, heat pumps and boilers.
method: Propose constrained design changes using simulation history and structured memory.
Evaluate each configuration with a year-long simulation and a 25-year net present cost objective.
Keep successful changes and automatically revert unsuccessful ones using git, recording an auditable trace.
evidence_signal: On one measured-load building case study, agents received 50 simulations per run versus 300 for baselines; their best cost was 1.20% below TPE and 0.23% below the evolution strategy.
watch_item: Results concern integrated building energy design—not solar-cell device optimization—and generalization beyond the single case study remains unestablished.
paper_title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization
